target_customer: Engineering and SRE teams that pay for hosted load testing, Playwright end-to-end testing and monitoring on top of an open source tool
problem: Teams need to know their APIs and apps hold up under load and stay reliable in production, and existing tools like JMeter are heavy, GUI and XML based. Artillery offers a developer-friendly load testing CLI and a cloud service for distributed tests.
business_model: Open source core (MPL 2.0 per a search summary) plus paid Artillery Cloud SaaS
product_category: Load testing and E2E testing developer tools

founders.name: Hassy Veldstra
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him an SRE and open source developer turned founder. InfoWorld (Mar 2021) says he built a chat app and created the tool as a solo project starting 2016. Education and employers not found.

competitors.name: Apache JMeter
competitors.what: Long established open source load testing tool with GUI and XML scripts
competitors.traction_then: The most features, plugins and integrations per Grafana review; called losing share to newer tools

competitors.name: k6
competitors.what: Open source load testing tool with JavaScript scripting
competitors.traction_then: Reviewed alongside Artillery in a March 2020 Grafana review; reviewer is a k6 creator

competitors.name: Locust
competitors.what: Open source Python-scripted load testing tool with distributed mode and web UI

competitors.name: Gatling
competitors.what: Actively maintained Scala-based load testing tool
competitors.traction_then: Described as very competent and actively developed

technical_complexity.rationale: Load generation, protocol support and distributed serverless execution on cloud infrastructure; a small team built the open source tool, with the distributed cloud runner the harder part.

defensibility.rationale: Open source with strong rivals (k6 later joined Grafana); test scripts create some lock-in but many alternatives exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors kept growing; no source found of one copying or buying Artillery, which remains independent.

market_need_then: Developers had adopted DevOps and SRE practices and wanted code-based load testing instead of GUI tools; the project already had traction as open source before YC (Grafana reviewed it in 2020).

identity.logo: An SVG logo exists in package READMEs; design not described
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, concise, outcome focused: 'Keep production reliable, customers happy, and pagers silent' (company site)

branding.community_and_virality: Open source project with a GitHub repository (company site cites 8.9K stars) and GitHub Discussions; an InfoWorld interview and an Open Source Startup Podcast episode cover it.

brand_strength.rationale: Known among developers through the open source project and press such as InfoWorld, but the name is generic and shared with other projects.

pivots.to: Platform with Playwright E2E testing and load testing, with monitoring planned
pivots.why: Expansion visible on the company site; reasons not stated

outcome_analysis: Artillery is active and independent. The open source tool dates to 2016 and had developer traction before YC S21. Public trackers put total funding around $2M with Y Combinator, Boldstart and others but no round was verified. The company now sells a cloud product and adds Playwright testing, with a team of five on the YC page, suggesting steady lean growth rather than a large raise.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights shows 2.1M over four rounds with a seed in April 2023, FundedIQ shows 2.0M in Aug 2021, Seedtable shows a 130k pre-seed in July 2021. None confirmed by company or press so no rounds are recorded. Company YC post (Aug 2021) says funding not disclosed. YC lists founded 2021 but the project began in 2016. One aggregator naming Nora Jones as founder is ignored as wrong. Artillery described as slow in the 2020 Grafana review by a k6 creator, so competitor descriptions are biased. Recorded rounds rest on a single database each (Seedtable pre-seed, CB Insights seed of April 2023 with no amount). CB Insights total of 2.1M over four rounds and FundedIQ 2.0M in Aug 2021 are not itemised, so the gap is unresolved; no press confirms any amount.
